_: Shared behavioural table for the Chart of Accounts' five refusals — see scripts/check-mirrors.js check 10. `jayhind-client-back/src/const/ledger.const.ts` enforces them; `jayhindi-client-front/src/utils/ledger-rules.util.ts` states them on screen so an operator reads the reason instead of meeting a 400. Both must answer every expanded row with the SAME SENTENCE, and both must match the sentence stated here — so a wording one side quietly improved, and a rule both sides forgot together, are different failures.
__regions: A case's `given` holds ARRAYS: every combination is expanded and compared, so a case is a statement about a REGION of the fact space rather than one row. The regions of each rule below partition it exactly — 182 comparisons over 22 hand-written cases. Ordering matters inside a rule and the cases say which arm they are about.
__unknown: `hasPostings` / `subtreeHasPostings` may be `null` here, meaning ABSENT — the browser cannot know whether a ledger has posted, and inventing a guess would produce a refusal that is sometimes wrong. Both sides must then answer `null` (allowed) and let the server, which does know, refuse with the same sentence. That equivalence is a rule, not an accident, so it is in the table.

messages.no-nature: This group has no account nature, so a ledger under it would have no side of the books to report on. File it under an Asset, Liability, Income or Expense group instead.
messages.control-group: Sundry Debtors and Sundry Creditors hold one ledger per trading party, created with the party itself — a ledger made by hand here would carry a balance that no outstanding or statement report could attribute to anybody. Add the party instead, or use a sub-group.
messages.children: This group has ${childGroupCount} sub-group(s). Move or delete them first.
messages.ledgers: This group holds ${ledgerCount} ledger(s). Move or delete them first.
messages.primary-delete: A primary group is part of the Balance Sheet and Profit & Loss structure and cannot be deleted.
messages.predefined-delete: This is a predefined group and cannot be deleted. Tally treats its own 28 the same way.
messages.primary-move: A primary group is part of the Balance Sheet and Profit & Loss structure and cannot be moved.
messages.cycle: A group cannot be moved inside its own subtree.
messages.group-nature: This group already has posted entries, and the destination sits under a different account nature — moving it would re-sign figures that have already been reported. Create the group in the new place and use it going forward instead.
messages.ledger-system-move: This is a system ledger. Where it sits decides how statutory figures are reported, so it is placed by the chart of accounts rather than moved by hand.
messages.ledger-nature: This ledger already has posted entries, and the destination sits under a different account nature — moving it would re-sign figures that have already been reported. Move it while it is empty, or leave it where its history was posted.
messages.ledger-system-delete: This is a system ledger and cannot be deleted. Deactivate it instead if it is no longer used.
messages.ledger-posted: This ledger carries posted entries and cannot be deleted. Deactivate it instead — the entries that name it must stay readable.

placement.why: the nature arm is asked FIRST, so Suspense A/c answers about its missing nature even when it is also a control group — a ledger with no side of the books cannot be paired with a trx_groups twin, whose accountNature is NOT NULL
in this ERP a debtor/creditor ledger IS a party (D3): one made by hand carries no partyUserId, so its balance sits on the Balance Sheet and appears in no receivables report at all

a ledger that already IS a party belongs under a control group — that is where D3 put every one of them. Moving a posted one across the two is refused by the move rule, whose message describes the real problem

Tally allows a ledger under any group, primary ones included, and so does this — an operator who wants a Fixed Assets ledger without inventing a sub-group gets one. isPrimary is deliberately NOT a refusal

groupDelete.why: the counts come before the structural refusals because they are the answers an operator can act on — and acc_groups.parentId is RESTRICT, so an unguarded delete surfaces as a 409 naming a constraint
this group's OWN ledgers, never the subtree's — GET /acc-groups/tree carries the same count per node so the screen can say it without asking
Tally's 15 primaries ARE the sections of the Balance Sheet and the P&L
structural rows shipped as an editable master is how a company ends up without a Sales head (F8)
an empty group somebody made is theirs to remove

groupReparent.why: moving a primary is not a re-parent, it is a different chart of accounts
a tree that became a ring makes a roll-up either walk for ever or truncate silently, and the second is the one that ships
nature is inherited and denormalised onto every descendant, so the move re-signs figures already reported — money between the P&L and the Balance Sheet with both still balancing (D-19)

an empty subtree has nothing to re-sign, which is what makes this a rule about postings rather than about natures — and an ABSENT count is the browser's honest 'not known here', answered by the server
a pure re-filing, postings and all — and isSystem does NOT block a move: the seeded 28 may not be deleted or renamed, but their placement is a choice Tally allows too

ledgerMove.why: where a statutory head sits is what decides whether input GST reports as an asset or a liability (NATURE_CHANGING_KEYS, ₹1,54,85,553 across the development companies) — a declared decision, not an operator's
D3's declared parity exception happening again, one party at a time, with no plan row and no human review behind it
an empty ledger has nothing to re-sign; an absent count is the server's question
the ledger appears under a different group on the Trial Balance and its figures keep their sign and their statement

ledgerDelete.why: refused whether or not it has posted — F8's argument about structural rows in an editable master
journal_lines.ledgerId is a real FK and every statement that printed it names it — such a ledger deactivates (BUG-0059's rule generalised)
an unposted ledger somebody made by mistake is theirs to remove; an absent count is the server's question
